decisions.reason: The existing message-672 MODIFY already captures the per-mint commission rule, no-referral visibility, historical backfill, cross-surface accuracy, and ticket-to-commission consistency; no additional change is required.

The existing message-672 MODIFY captures no-referral ticket visibility and historical backfill, while the prior state already requires one accounted ticket per primary mint and registration of randomly assigned tickets.

The source clarifies operational accounting and metadata accuracy rather than requesting FAQ changes; the existing FAQ state already says no-referral commissions and Small Block tickets go to a random existing holder.
Ticket and commission accounting for primary mints does not change which NFT state or entitlements transfer during a secondary sale.
The distinction between code-used and no-referral mints does not alter the NFT mint number as its permanent referral code or any referral-code display surface.
The source concerns primary-mint reward accounting and does not change the flat secondary-sale royalty, token standard, or marketplace enforcement policy.
The source reports missing reward records for completed mints but does not change the rule for displaying NFTs actually owned by the connected user.
The existing message-672 MODIFY captures one $5 commission for every completed no-referral primary mint, and the prior state already specifies random allocation to an existing NFT holder.
The accounting expectations for twelve completed mints do not change the collection's unlimited-mint NFT ebook model.
Reward accounting and NFT-attribute consistency do not change the View Book action or its owner-only visibility rule.
The source concerns accounting attributes rather than NFT cover visibility, sizing, or image presentation.
The statement that twelve mints were completed is context for expected reward totals, not a change to the existing rule that public mint statistics count only successful mints.
